LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 15.3.1 TYPES OF SENTENCES: INTERROGATIVE SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, part of Strand 1 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we ask questions? 2. How do we answer questions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a text online or offline on varied topics including tourist attraction sites in Africa,

2. identify interrogative sentences such as WH- questions, Yes/ No questions and alternative questions,

3. identify question tags from a given text and practise asking and answering them,

4. form interrogatives and tag questions and display them on a graphic organiser, with peers,

5. use interrogatives in a role play relevant to the theme of tourism in Africa,

6. read a dialogue featuring interrogatives and tag questions, with peers,

7. search the internet for more examples of question tags and interrogatives. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a text online or offline on varied topics including tourist attraction sites in Africa,
2. identify interrogative sentences such as WH- questions, Yes/ No questions and alternative questions,
3. identify question tags from a given text and practise asking and answering them,
4. form interrogatives and tag questions and display them on a graphic organiser, with peers,
5. use interrogatives in a role play relevant to the theme of tourism in Africa,
6. read a dialogue featuring interrogatives and tag questions, with peers,
7. search the internet for more examples of question tags and interrogatives. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: It is developed as the learner accomplishes different tasks while dramatising and

recording sections of the short story that reflect real life experiences.

• Self- efficacy: It is sharpened as the learner documents successes achieved while constructing different types of

interrogatives.

Values:
Respect: It is emphasised as the learner appreciates others while engaging in a dialogue featuring interrogative sentences and

question tags.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Problem solving: It is promoted as the learner asks and answers questions on tourism in Africa.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Social Studies, Religious Education and Mathematics involve asking and answering questions.
